motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain Citg, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.130(a) Residential Water Rights Requirements Eagle Mountain 0ity Council Meeting - January 16,2024 Page 16 of 20 Citg Engineer Chris Trustg presented the item. With recentlg adopted changes to Municipal Code that include reduced landscape requirements for front and side gards, this subsequent amendment is proposed to reduce water required for development to reflect the decreased landscape requirements. The recommended water rights requirements are based onTO% of the total landscaped portion of the lot being planted with sod with the remaining 3O% being planted with xeriscape or other drought- tolerant landscaping that conforms to Municipal Code. An adjustment is also being made to the per- acre water requirement for outdoor use to account for watering inefficiencies. The per-acre water requirement will go from 2.5 acre-feet per irrigable acre to 3.2 acre-feet per irrigable acre. Based on recent evaluations of a random sampling of existing Citg residents, the indoor requirements will be reduced from O.53 to O.34 acre-feet to reflect a more accurate use that the Citg has seen on the sgstem. Mang cities currentlg require O.3 acre-feet for indoor use; however, the Citg staff recommendation is to require slightlg more. This will ensure adequate water rights are provided to account for inefficiencg in the Citg's deliverg sgstem, as well as help account for losses between water production and point of sale with the landscape irrigation sgstem. These changes will reduce the per lot water required to be dedicated to the Citg at plat recordation. Discussion considered multifamilg water requirements being 80% lower than other housing tgpes potentiallg not reflecting water usage of units with the same number of bedrooms as single-familg homes. and the abilitg of developers to sell water shares if theg over-purchased water to meet previous standards. Magor Westmoreland opened the public hearing at 9:26 p.m. As there were no comments, he closed the hearing
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section lZ35.O3O Land Use Table and 17.55.120 Tables until the Hotel Feasibility Study Is completed. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion. The motion passed with a vote of 4:1.
motions.headline: Hotel height and parking rules put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed changes that would let hotels rise above the city's 50-foot limit and provide fewer parking stalls, waiting until the hotel feasibility study is finished.
motions.impact: No hotel was approved or blocked here. The current rules stand, so a developer wanting a four-story hotel still runs into the height cap and the stall-per-bed count until the study comes back.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.08, Form of Government and Section 2.15J20 Mayor Pro Tempore and Council Assignments Councilmember Wood explained that the proposed ordinance, requested by Councilmember Wright and himself, codifies Eagle Mountain City's six-member council form of government and establishes that the powers of municipal government are vested in the City Council, consisting of five Councilmembers and the Mayor. The City Council shall make the decisions for the City with a vote and approval in an open and public meeting. The ordinance further clarifies the executive and staff powers and identifies that, on an annual basis, the City Council shall elect a Mayor Pro Tempore from the body of the elected City Councilmembers and will discuss and make assignments for representation and support for the citizens of the City. They worked with the City Attorney to ensure that the amendment clarified State Code rather than altering or removing authority from anyone. Discussion ensued regarding the following: o Additional changes to the language in the amendment; . Concerns that, "2.08.030. Council Administration. No one member of the city council or the mayor shall make decisions for the city council nor shall any member of the city council, knowinglg or otherwise, give the perception to an organization or individual citizen that they represent the full body of the city council without the city council's vote and approval in an open and public meeting," could impede staff and the Mayor from functioning in certain aspects of their roles or be misinterpreted, leading to accusations and possible punitive measures; . The desire to empower staff to explore all options and solutions without fear of retribution. o Changing 2.OB.060. Adoption of Policies to "No new policies, code, ordinance, or resolution shall be created andenacted by mayor or staff without written request and then consent of the majority vote of city council in an open and public meeting;" . Confusion over the impact of the standards on the procurement code; o Wording differences between the amendment and State Code; o Benefits and complications should the Mayor and Counciljointlg make liaison assignments; and . Adding the process for nomination and approval of the Mayor Pro Tempore to the proposed standards for claritg. Mr. Draper stated that the proposed changes to EMMC 2.08.030, while good in principle and practice, are an addition to, rather than a clarification of State statute and would constitute a substantive change to the law impacting the Mayor's powers, duties, and functions thus necessitating certain procedural requirements to be followed when voting on the change. When the Mayor speaks, unless he emphaticallg states that he is speaking for himself, others could assume he is speaking for the City as a whole. He recommended adding a section that the legislative intent is to codifg and clarify existing standards rather than to make substantive changes

motions.headline: Less water required from builders per lot
motions.summary: The council cut the water a builder must hand the city per lot, dropping the indoor share from 0.53 to 0.34 acre-feet, and ordered a study of apartment water use.
motions.impact: Builders dedicating water rights for new subdivisions now hand over less, matching the smaller lawns the city already requires. Your own bill and service stay the same. The apartment study may bring the question back.

motions.impact: Nothing changes for you yet. The rules govern how councilmembers, staff and the mayor may speak for the city, and the reworked version was set to return on February 6.
